01.r: Turns from the case of Zelophehad's daughters to a law for all Israel.
01.n: The verse opens with the people addressed, ahead of the verb: 'and to the sons of Israel you shall speak'.

02.n: STEPBible tags this occurrence with the sense 'descendant, people'. The BSB says 'the Israelites'.

04.r: Moses is to announce the ruling to the people.

05.r: Introduces the words of the law itself.
05.n: An infinitive, literally 'to say'; it works like a colon or opening quotation mark.

06.r: Any Israelite head of a family.

07.r: Sets out the case the law covers.
07.n: The Hebrew puts 'a man' first: 'a man, if he dies'.

08.r: The owner of the land dies.

09.r: A son, the usual heir of family land.
09.n: The word carries the Hebrew 'and', given here as the plain 'and' before 'he has'.

10.r: No son is living to inherit.
10.n: A word meaning 'nothing, there is not'; with 'to him' it is the Hebrew way of saying 'he has no'. The brief's lexicon lists 'to have not (of possession)' among its senses.

11.r: The dead man, as the one without a son.
11.n: Literally 'to him'; counted with 'he has no'.

12.r: The community must see that the land goes to the daughter.
12.n: The causative form of the verb 'pass over': literally 'you shall cause to pass over'. It is plural: the people as a whole carry out the transfer.
t: then ye shall cause ... to pass
then ye shall cause ... to pass
then ye shall cause ... to pass
then ye have caused ... to pass over

13.r: Marks 'his inheritance' as the object of the verb.
13.n: This small word marks a definite direct object and has no English equivalent; it is counted here with 'you shall pass on'.

14.n: Gesenius notes this noun is often used of the territory assigned to each tribe.

15.r: The daughter becomes the heir when there is no son.

12.n: περιτίθημι, put around, confer upon: 'you shall confer his inheritance on his daughter'.
